_README: Rider ids that are variants of one person, and the id they belong to. CONSULTED AT INGEST: without this a re-ingest recreates every absorbed id straight from the scrape files, because the files still carry the old spelling — the same way the Dorsal placeholders came back. Lives outside the DB for that reason, like stage_notes.json and route_type_overrides.json. Produced by audit_rider_duplicates.py + merge_rider_duplicates.py; every entry carries the evidence for the claim, because a merge IS a claim and a wrong one fuses two careers invisibly. The `separated` section is the MIRROR of `aliases`: pairs a human examined and ruled DIFFERENT people. Without it audit_rider_duplicates.py re-proposes them on every run and the next --apply quietly re-merges a decision somebody already made.

rider/aaron-gammell.evidence: Unbound 2010/2011/2012, one rider. Two of his three registrations spell it GAMMEL (2011, 2012) against one Gammell (2010), so the source majority picks the canonical, not string length. A separate Jed Gammell rides Chequamegon with the double L and is a different person.

rider/alejandro-gomez.evidence: Both ids were created for one finisher of The Traka 360 by two sources that spell him differently: PCS's result page and the timer's own ranking. They are the same man because the finish times are identical to the second: 50596s in the 2024 edition, PCS rank 83. PCS's own slug is alejandro-gomez1, and PCS appends that digit only when the bare slug already belongs to someone else. Keeping our locally-minted `alejandro-gomez` would leave a name-shaped id for a rider PCS calls something else, which a later import of that OTHER Alejandro Gomez would land on. The PCS id survives even though it holds no result.

RESOLVED 2026-09-11 by counting EVENTS rather than records: Leadville 1997 spells it FOLLET and Chequamegon 1999 spells it Follet, against Follett at Leadville 1999 — 2 events to 1. The Leadville PDF is not an independent witness, it is the same Athlinks data. No outside source records him at all. Canonical greg-follet stands, now on evidence rather than on an alphabetical tie-break.

rider/mathieu-belanger-barette.evidence: Bélanger-Barrette, double R, confirmed by the UCI rider database plus Precision Hydration, Cycling Weekly, Velo, Reserve Wheels and FirstCycling. PCS spells it 'barette' and PCS IS WRONG; its slug was what link_gravel_riders matched on. The canonical therefore moves to the 0-result sportmaniacs identity, which is the only one spelling his name correctly — the opposite of what a most-results rule would pick. CONFIRMED SAME PERSON: PCS's own page for the misspelled slug gives a birth date of 3 August 1989, matching the press profile of Mathieu Bélanger-Barrette exactly. PCS has only the one page — /rider/mathieu-belanger-barrette is a 404 — so this is a single rider whose NAME PCS has wrong, not two riders. The upstream typo cannot be fixed from here and is recorded in DATA_SOURCES.md.

rider/tobias-morch-kongstad.evidence: CONFIRMED by outside sources, and the most consequential of the set: one elite career split across two ids. Tobias Morch Kongstad is Danish, born 14 September 1996 in Copenhagen, and rides for PAS Racing. Wikipedia files him as Tobias Kongstad, Cyclingnews's rider page as Tobias Morch Kongstad, and Groadio podcast ep.101 as Tobias Morch Kongstad. Our two ids hold exactly the career those sources describe: the full-name id has The Traka 360 2023 (2nd, club PAS Normal Studios) and 2024 (5th, PAS Racing); the short id has Unbound 2024 3rd, which Cyclingnews reports as his breakthrough, and The Traka 360 2025, which he won solo, plus Unbound 2025 and 2026, Big Sugar 2025 and Sea Otter 2026.

ernest-gilioli|ernest-gillioli.evidence: Wikipedia's 1926 Tour startlist has Gillioli at number 147 as a touriste-routier; its 1909 list has Gilioli at 157 as a lone rider. Two entries, two numbers, two categories. PCS dates Gilioli to 1885, making him 41 in 1926 — possible, but nothing asserts one man.
ernest-gilioli|ernest-gillioli.note: merged 2026-09-11 and reversed the same day

gilbert-desmet-i|gilbert-de-smet-ii.evidence: They share 93 stages and nobody rides a race twice. PCS's roman numerals separate two riders of one family; the hyphenation differs as well, which is why the name heuristic called them SAME.
gilbert-desmet-i|gilbert-de-smet-ii.note: never merged — refused by the share-a-stage test

giuseppe-bereta|giuseppe-beretta.evidence: Il Lombardia 1909 and Milan-San Remo 1934: 25 years, two different races, nothing in between. Placing 72nd in a professional classic at about 49 is not credible.
giuseppe-bereta|giuseppe-beretta.note: merged 2026-09-11 and reversed the same day

hugo-simon|simon-hugot.evidence: NOT the same person, despite an identical Traka 2024 finish time of 54014s. PCS's page reads 'Simon Hugo' with the team UVCA Troyes, and Hugo Simon is a real French rider with his own PCS page at that team. The official timer's 737-man field contains no Hugo Simon at all -- it has SIMON HUGOT (FR, club La Nuit Noire) at exactly that time, and Hugot has no PCS page. The likeliest reading is that PCS matched the finisher's name to the wrong rider in its own database, and the team it shows is that other rider's. Merging would fuse a French road rider's identity into a gravel finisher who is not him.

jonathan-homberg|jonathan-van-den-berg.evidence: NOT the same person, despite an identical Traka 2024 finish time of 51336s. Jonathan van den Berg is a real Dutch road professional, active 2022-2025, with his own PCS rider page; PCS's Traka 2024 page lists him. The timer's full 737-man field has no van den Berg anywhere -- at that exact time it has JONATHAN HOMBERG (DE), who has no PCS page. Same first name, different surname, different nationality. Same-second finishes are ordinary in a mass-start gravel race, so the shared time is not evidence of identity here; the pattern matches PCS mis-linking a finisher to an existing rider page.
